correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, the complete published row/column sign inequalities admit a mutually exhaustive facet-pair classification: same support Hamming-one only if n>=3, different parallel supports only if n>=3, and mixed row/column supports only if signs agree at the shared cell. Explicit strict two-active-facet witnesses prove inclusion; forced coordinate zeros or extra active independent facets exclude all remaining cases. Norms sqrt(n) and dot products 0,1,n-2 yield the listed interior angles and counts. Exact vertex-face affine-rank tests reproduce every pair for n=2,3,4 (120, 1128, 8128 pairs), but the geometric proof, not the tests, establishes the general case. The rare weight is asymptotically (2/3)2^(-n); inverse-trigonometric expansions give the two-atom scaled limit and mean excess.
risks: No independent mathematical audit; numeric rank calculations test small orders, and fail as an infinite proof by themselves.

value.rationale: The canonical signed Birkhoff family is a natural high-dimensional reflexive polytope with an exponential facet count. The complete Euclidean ridge-angle classification, all-order multiplicities, and scaled limiting law reveal a nonobvious separation between bulk near-right ridges and exponentially rare nearly-flat ridges; the sharp small-order exception and angle coalescence strengthen its natural geometric content. This is an exact all-dimension metric invariant and a motivated basis for later area-weighted curvature study, not a tiny numerical increment or arbitrary slice.
risks: No claimed area-weighted intrinsic-volume consequence or historical priority proof.
